processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2026-01-01..2026-09-09. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. Provincial subset - do not sum with national row. STATE-LEVEL documented absence during a national epidemic, which is the strongest kind of absence evidence: the assertion comes from the head of the national surveillance authority, is made about one named state while 35 others and the FCT were reporting, and explicitly addresses and rejects the concealment hypothesis. Surveillance is recorded as operational because NCDC's own IDSR and event-based surveillance were running nationwide throughout the 2026 epidemic and the DG was actively adjudicating state reporting quality. INTERPRETIVE LIMIT: this is nil REPORTING of cholera from Enugu to NCDC, not proven biological absence; the DG's own framing is 'yet to report a cholera case'. Arithmetic check: NCDC's 28 August 2026 briefing gives 35 states affected (index 41), and Nigeria has 36 states plus the FCT, so exactly one state and no more can be cholera-free on NCDC's own count - consistent with Enugu being that state. Confidence held at 0.55 because the statement reaches us through a Level 3 outlet rather than an NCDC publication. TR is the date of the report, not the end of the year: nothing is asserted about Enugu after 9 September 2026.

source: Dalhat MM et al. 2018, Pan African Medical Journal 30:5 - relaying Epidemiology Division, Federal Ministry of Health Nigeria unpublished national cholera surveillance, January 2004-December 2008
processing_notes: Source states: 'According to surveillance data obtained from the Epidemiology Division, Federal Ministry of Health, between January 2004 and December 2008, outbreaks of cholera have been reported in 12 out of the 36 States in the country with 74,881 cases and 1,387 reported deaths (Unpublished data).' - interpreted as 74881 sCh cases, 1387 deaths. REPLACES retracted index 6, which carried these same figures against metadata index 8 'Federal Ministry of Health Nigeria' whose only URL was the bare domain https://www.health.gov.ng - an unverifiable citation. The primary text was located by a Europe PMC full-text search on the literal string '74,881' and is Dalhat et al., Pan African Medical Journal 2018;30:5 (PMC6093587), which attributes the figure to FMoH Epidemiology Division UNPUBLISHED data. [AGENT 5 CONFLICT ADJUDICATION 2026-09-21] THIS FIGURE IS 4.5x THE AUTHORITATIVE ANNUAL SERIES FOR THE SAME WINDOW. The WHO Annual Cholera Report series carried in ./data/NGA/cholera_data_jhu.csv gives 2004 3186/185, 2005 4477/174, 2006 2028/127, 2007 1661/48, 2008 5410/247 - a five-year total of 16,762 cases and 781 deaths, CFR 4.66 percent, against this row's 74,881 and 1,387, CFR 1.85 percent. Both figures are recorded and NEITHER IS AVERAGED. ADJUDICATION: the WHO annual series is PRIMARY for 2004-2008 and this row is NON-PRIMARY, downweighted from 0.7 to 0.4. Rule applied: WHO official over ministry, published over unpublished, and a series over a single relayed aggregate. AN ARITHMETIC FINDING THAT MAY EXPLAIN THE GAP: 74,881 does not match the WHO 2004-2008 sum but it matches the WHO 2004-2010 sum of 74,909 to within 28 cases, 0.04 percent. The 2009 and 2010 epidemic years (13,691 and 44,456 cases) are almost exactly the missing volume, so the FMoH internal aggregation most likely ran to 2010 and the window stated in the 2018 paper is too short - or the FMoH series used a broader acute-watery-diarrhoea case definition. The deaths do not follow the same pattern (WHO 2004-2010 = 2,924 against 1,387 here), so this is a hypothesis, not a resolution, and the row is deliberately left on its printed 2004-2008 period rather than silently redated. National total - includes states not individually listed; do not sum with the nested sub-national rows 410, 411, 412, 413, 641 or with index 1181.

processing_notes: Source states: 'As of 31 May 2026, a total of 237 new cholera cases were reported.' - interpreted as 237 sCh cases. SINGLE-DAY INCIDENCE, not a cumulative. This is one of very few true daily incidence values in the Nigerian file and it is additive rather than nested, so it can be used directly. The source flags the figure with a footnote reading 'still updating linelist', so it is provisional and is likely a slight undercount; confidence reduced from the Level 1 floor to 0.8 for that reason. The same document records 274 new admissions and 249 discharges in the 24 hours to 31 May 2026, with 362 patients then in care - admissions are NOT recorded as cases here because admissions and surveillance-reported cases are different denominators. Provincial subset - do not sum with national rows, and do not sum with the nested cumulative Borno rows.

source: UNICEF Nigeria Humanitarian Flash Update Cholera Borno State 7 June 2026
processing_notes: Source states: 'As of 4th June 2026, 7,233 suspected Cholera cases with 46 deaths (26 facility-based and 20 community deaths) have been reported (overall Case Fatality Rate (CFR) of 0.6%).' - interpreted as 7233 sCh cases, 46 deaths. SECOND, EARLIER CUT DATE INSIDE AN ALREADY-USED SOURCE. The same UNICEF flash update of 7 June 2026 carries a headline Borno figure of 8,457 cases / 85 deaths as of 7 June (already recorded as Index 32) and, in the epidemiological narrative, this distinct 4 June figure. Both are printed in the same document and neither supersedes the other; they are three days apart. Internal consistency check: 46/7233 = 0.64 per cent, matching the printed CFR of 0.6 per cent. The jump from 46 deaths on 4 June to 85 on 7 June reflects retrospective addition of community deaths (20 to 32) and facility deaths (26 to 53) rather than three days of mortality. NESTED CUMULATIVE from 1 May 2026 - do not sum with the other Borno cumulative rows. Provincial subset - do not sum with national rows.

source: International Medical Corps, Nigeria Cholera Outbreak Situation Report #2, 4 June 2026 (citing Borno State Ministry of Health)
processing_notes: Source states: 'According to the State Ministry of Health, 6,078 suspected cases and 65 deaths had been reported as of June 3.' - interpreted as 6078 sCh cases, 65 deaths. Borno State Ministry of Health cumulative, relayed by International Medical Corps. NESTED CUMULATIVE from 1 May 2026 - do not sum with other Borno cumulative rows. Sits between two neighbouring snapshots already in the file and is consistent with neither being wrong: Daily Trust/MSF gives 4,204/39 to 2 June (Index 90) and UNICEF gives 7,233/46 to 4 June (Index 1513). The three are on different reporting streams - MSF treatment-centre data, the UNICEF/EOC line list, and the State MoH PHEOC count - so the apparent jump from 4,204 on 2 June to 6,078 on 3 June to 7,233 on 4 June is stream difference plus retrospective line-list updating, not three days of true incidence. Deaths are also inconsistent across the three streams (39, 65, 46) and must not be differenced. Geography at this date: 12 LGAs, 40 wards, 138 settlements. Provincial subset - do not sum with national rows.

source: International Medical Corps, Nigeria Cholera Outbreak Situation Report #3, 6 July 2026 (citing Borno State Ministry of Health)
processing_notes: Source states: 'As of July 5, the State Ministry of Health had reported 28,082 suspected cases and 143 deaths.' - interpreted as 28082 sCh cases, 143 deaths. Borno State Ministry of Health cumulative, relayed by International Medical Corps. NESTED CUMULATIVE from 1 May 2026 - do not sum with other Borno cumulative rows. This fills the largest remaining hole in the Borno 2026 cumulative series, which previously jumped from 13,234/108 on 18 June (Index 35) to 35,500/198 on 12 July (Index 1406); the 5 July value of 28,082/143 shows that roughly three-fifths of that rise happened before 5 July. source: UNICEF/WHO joint statement, cholera outbreak in 11 Nigerian States, 1 September 2010 (citing Government of Nigeria officials)
processing_notes: Source states: 'Government officials say that at 30 August, 6,400 cases of cholera had been reported since the beginning of the outbreak, including 352 deaths.' - interpreted as 6400 sCh cases, 352 deaths. First within-year national cut date for the 2010 Nigerian epidemic in this file, which previously held only the 41,787/1,716 annual total (Index 7). TL set to 2010-07-01 because the source says 'since the beginning of the outbreak' and both ReliefWeb and the IFRC bulletin date the outbreak onset to July 2010; the true onset day is not printed, so TL is an approximation and the row should be read as a cumulative-to-30-August figure rather than a July-August increment. Eleven states named as affected: Sokoto, Katsina, Jigawa, Bauchi, Yobe, Gombe, Borno, Adamawa, Taraba (north), Rivers and Cross River (south). The source also prints state CFRs of 10.2 per cent for Jigawa and 9.6 per cent for Yobe, which are not entered as rows because no state case counts accompany them. CONFLICT: the IFRC information bulletin of 2 September 2010 gives 'over 7,000 persons with over 232 deaths since July 2010' for essentially the same moment - the case counts are compatible but the death counts are not, and neither is averaged. National row - do not sum with the state rows for 2010. NESTED within the annual total, do not sum with Index 7.

source: IFRC Nigeria Cholera Information Bulletin No. 1, 2 September 2010
processing_notes: Source states: 'A cholera outbreak has been reported in some states in Nigeria mostly in the northern part of the country with over 7,000 persons with over 232 deaths since July 2010.' - interpreted as 7000 sCh cases, 232 deaths. LOWER BOUNDS: the source says 'over 7,000' and 'over 232', so both values are floors, not point estimates; confidence reduced accordingly. CONFLICT WITH THE PARALLEL UNICEF/WHO FIGURE, documented not resolved: UNICEF and WHO, citing Government officials, give 6,400 cases and 352 deaths at 30 August 2010 (Index immediately preceding), three days earlier. The case counts are reconcilable on a rising epidemic curve; the death counts move in the wrong direction (352 down to 232), so the two streams are counting deaths differently - most likely facility-only versus facility-plus-community. Neither is averaged and neither is suppressed. National row - do not sum with 2010 state rows and do not sum with the annual total (Index 7).

source: UNICEF Nigeria Cholera and Floods Situation Report No. 5, 23 September - 4 October 2010
processing_notes: Source states: 'a total of 2,137 new cases of cholera and 95 deaths from the disease were reported by six states during the reporting period' - interpreted as 2137 sCh cases, 95 deaths. TRUE PERIOD INCREMENT, not a cumulative: these are NEW cases and deaths reported during 23 September - 4 October 2010 only, so this row is additive and can be used directly as incidence. One of very few non-nested national observations for 2010. The source cautions that 'Information and data collection since the last sitrep has been erratic, largely due to the national holidays', so the figure is likely an undercount of true incidence in that window. Reported by six states; the epidemic also spread to six new local government areas during the period. National row - do not sum with 2010 state rows, and do not sum with the cumulative national rows (Index 7 and the 30 August, 2 September and 22 October cumulatives).

source: UN News Centre, Nigeria experiencing worst cholera outbreak in years, 22 October 2010 (citing UNICEF)
processing_notes: Source states: 'Nigeria is in the midst of its worst cholera outbreak in recent years, with nearly 40,000 cases and more than 1,500 deaths reported since the start of the year' - interpreted as 40000 sCh cases, 1500 deaths. APPROXIMATE FIGURES: 'nearly 40,000' is an upper bound and 'more than 1,500 deaths' is a lower bound, so 40000/1500 are rounded values not exact counts; confidence reduced accordingly. Consistent with the year-end national total of 41,787 cases and 1,716 deaths (Index 7), implying about 1,800 further cases and 200 further deaths after 22 October 2010. The source gives a national CFR of 4.5 per cent and state CFRs of 20 per cent in Plateau, 17 per cent in Sokoto and 11 per cent in Gombe; those are not entered as rows because no accompanying state case counts are printed. National row - NESTED within the annual total, do not sum with Index 7 or with 2010 state rows.

source: Sule IB et al. 2017, Descriptive epidemiology of a cholera outbreak in Kaduna State, Northwest Nigeria, 2014, Pan African Medical Journal 27:172
processing_notes: Source states: 'A total of 1468 case-patients and 54 deaths were recorded, giving a case fatality rate (CFR) of 3.68%.' - interpreted as 1468 sCh cases, 54 deaths. Peer-reviewed reconstruction of the 2014 Kaduna State cholera outbreak. PERIOD DERIVATION: the paper states 'The outbreak started from the first epidemic week of 2014 and lasted over 33 weeks', so TL is set to 1 January 2014 and TR to 17 August 2014 (end of epi week 33); exact first and last case dates are not printed, so the period is an epi-week approximation. ARITHMETIC: the seven-LGA table sums to exactly 1,468 cases and exactly 54 deaths, matching the printed state total, so the decomposition is internally complete. Seven of Kaduna's 23 LGAs were affected: Chikun, Giwa, Igabi, Kaduna North, Kaduna South, Soba and Zaria. DATING CORRECTION FOR AN EXISTING ROW: Index 455 carries the same 1,468 cases and 54 deaths for Kaduna but dated 2013-12-01 to 2014-01-01, taken from the Charnley et al. 2022 compilation. That is the same outbreak mis-dated; the primary field-epidemiology paper places it across epi weeks 1-33 of 2014, not in December 2013. The two rows must NOT be treated as separate outbreaks or summed. State row - do not sum with the seven LGA rows from the same source, which decompose it exactly.
